Pairwise comparisons of a parameter between growth curves

Source: R/pairwise.R
pairwise.Rd

Compares a parameter of the population curves (random effects at zero) between every pair of rows of newdata, e.g. the treatment levels: the difference of the parameter on the scale of its link, its standard error from the covariance of the fixed effects, a Wald test of no difference, and a confidence interval. With b1type="rate" in gcTMB, b1 is the maximum growth rate, and pairwise(fit, newdata, "b1") compares the maximum growth rates.

Usage

pairwise(x, newdata, parm = "b1", adjust = "tukey", level = 0.95, nsim = 1e+05)

# S3 method for class 'pairwise.gcTMB'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

newdata

Data frame. The values of the covariates in fform, one row for each curve to compare; the rows are named as in timeto.

parm

Character string. The parameter to compare, "b1" to "b5"

adjust

Character string. Adjustment for the number of pairs: "tukey" (default) for the single-step adjustment of the p-values and simultaneous confidence intervals, a method of p.adjust for adjusted p-values only, e.g. "holm", or "none"

level

Numeric between 0 and 1. The level of the confidence intervals

nsim

Integer. Number of simulations of the largest absolute test statistic for adjust="tukey"

digits

Integer. Number of significant digits

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class pairwise.gcTMB with a row for each pair: the estimated difference, its standard error, the test statistic, the p-value and the confidence limits, with the ratio and its limits for the log link.

Details

The tests use t quantiles with small-sample inference (gcTMBcontrol), and normal quantiles otherwise. By default (adjust="tukey"), the p-values and the confidence intervals are adjusted by the single-step method, the generalisation of Tukey's honestly significant differences to any covariance of the estimates (Hothorn, Bretz and Westfall, 2008, the default of the multcomp package): they use the distribution of the largest absolute test statistic of all the pairs, given the correlations of the differences, so that the intervals cover all the differences simultaneously with probability level. This distribution is simulated, with nsim draws, which gives the adjusted p-values to about 0.002 for the default; the simulation has its own seed and leaves the random number generator as it was. The other methods of p.adjust, e.g. "holm", adjust the p-values only, and the confidence intervals are then not adjusted. For a parameter with the log link, the differences are log ratios, and the ratios with their confidence limits are given as well. Whether all the curves have the same value of the parameter is tested by a likelihood ratio test of the models with and without the covariates of the parameter, see anova.gcTMB.

References

Hothorn, T., Bretz, F. and Westfall, P. (2008). Simultaneous inference in general parametric models. Biometrical Journal 50, 346-363.

Examples

FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
# b1 as the maximum growth rate, on the log scale: differences of log rates
fit <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, data=FabaHeights25, b1type="rate", link=c(b1="log"))
pairwise(fit, newdata=data.frame(trt=levels(FabaHeights25$trt)), parm="b1")
#> Pairwise differences of b1 (maximum growth rate) on the scale of its log link:
#> 
#>                   Estimate Std.Error t value p.value   lower     upper ratio

#> trt=0.1 - trt=0.8 -0.06441    0.0332  -1.940  0.3009 -0.1559  0.027119 0.938
